Your Turn My Turn poster

April Greiman’s 3-D poster for a furniture design symposium at the Pacific Design Center: red and cyan type, dot screens, and wedges in a tilted, layered field.

Source

Context

The People’s Graphic Design Archive lists the poster as offset lithography, 24 × 36 in, for PDC2 Pacific Design Center / Westweek, and says it was a 3-D poster issued with glasses. People’s Graphic Design Archive, second record.

The poster names the event “The International Contract Furniture Design Symposium during WestWeek”, 18 and 19 March, Pacific Design Center, Los Angeles.

Observed

  • “Your Turn” and “My Turn” are set in a heavy italic grotesque at a slight tilt, each letter printed twice in dark red and cyan with an offset, as in anaglyph 3-D.
  • Small copies of “turn” and “you” float upside down and mirrored around the main words.
  • A panel of coarse dark-red dot screen fills the upper left. A field of red, white, and cyan spray dots spreads over a dark panel at the right.
  • Yellow and blue wedges and a black diagonal band cross the sheet. A red-grey photograph of the Earth sits at the lower left.
  • “1 9 8 3” is set as separate numerals stepping up across the dark panel.
  • Sponsor lists are set small on a yellow panel at an angle; the event details at the lower left are flush left in blue and pink italics, each line stepped to the right.
  • “P D C 2” sits in small separate squares at the top left.

Why it belongs

The poster shows how Greiman’s California work adds colour and depth to Weingart’s structure: the dot screens and wedges stay, but the palette moves to cyan, pink, and yellow, and the overprint becomes a literal 3-D effect.

Borrow

Print a display word twice in two colours with a small offset.

Space out a year into single numerals that step across a panel.

Tilt a small-print list as a block and keep its lines parallel to the panel edge.
